_meta: Two tool-call failures, each given both as a raw Python TRACEBACK and as a STRUCTURED error, used to show why a harness should return structured errors to the model (and to its own retry logic) instead of the raw traceback. When a tool call fails, the naive harness catches the exception and passes the raw traceback string straight back. A traceback is a large blob of internal file paths and stack frames with no machine-readable field the harness can branch on -- so the harness cannot programmatically tell whether the failure is worth retrying, and the model is handed noise. A STRUCTURED error carries the fields that actually drive a decision: a stable code, a short human message, a retryable flag, an optional retry_after_s, and a hint the model can act on. failures[0] is a transient rate-limit (retryable true, wait 2s and retry the same call); failures[1] is a permanent bad-argument error (retryable false, the model must fix the argument -- retrying unchanged will fail forever). With the structured flag the harness retries the transient one and does NOT retry the permanent one; with only the traceback it has no flag and a blanket policy mishandles at least one. The structured errors are also far smaller than the tracebacks. failures is the fixture; the raw-vs-structured sizes, the retryable extraction, and the retry decisions are computed.
